decisions.question: e-743

source.question: e-743
source.value:
The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=a$ is given by

$$
P_4(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x-a) + \dfrac{f''(a)}{2!}(x-a)^2 + \dfrac{f'''(a)}{3!}(x-a)^3 + \dfrac{f^{(4)}(a)}{4!}(x-a)^4.
$$

Here, we have $a=\dfrac{\pi}{2},$ so

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{4}(x) & =f(\frac{\pi }{2})+{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})(x-\frac{\pi }{2})+\frac{{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{2!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2} \\  & \,\,\,\,+\frac{{f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{3!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{3}+\frac{{f}^{(4)}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{4!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

So we need to work out $f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right),$ $f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right),$ $f''\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right),$ $f'''\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and $f^{(4)}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x & ⟹ &  & f(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =0 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-1 \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =0 \\ {f}^{(4)}(x) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{(4)}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P_4(x)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{4}(x) & =1-\frac{1}{2!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}+\frac{1}{4!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{4} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{2}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}+\frac{1}{24}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

source.value:
The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=0$ is given by

$$
P_4(x) = 1+2x-3x^2+4x^3-5x^4.
$$

What is $f^{(4)}(0)?$

decisions.question: e-744

source.question: e-744
source.value:
The coefficient of $x^4$ is given by $\dfrac{f^{(4)}(0)}{4!}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{(4)}(0)}{4!} & =-5 \\ \frac{{f}^{(4)}(0)}{24} & =-5 \\ {f}^{(4)}(0) & =-120.\end{aligned}
$$
